canonical_name: Poisson formula for the two-dimensional wave equation
canonical_statement: Let c > 0. For sufficiently regular initial displacement f and velocity g on R^2, the classical solution of u_tt = c^2 Delta u with u(x,0)=f(x) and u_t(x,0)=g(x) is the time derivative of the Poisson disk integral of f plus the Poisson disk integral of g; the exact regularity, support, time domain, and uniqueness class remain to be frozen in the statement phase.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: c t : Real, x : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 2), f g u real-valued; all live in Lean universe 0. Function spaces and differentiability classes are deliberately unresolved.
quantifiers: f and g on R^2 with sufficient regularity
hypotheses: u is a classical solution of u_tt = c^2 Delta u
regularity/integrability assumptions sufficient for disk integrals and differentiation
conclusion: u equals the two-dimensional Poisson integral representation, with the initial conditions recovered at t=0 and uniqueness in the selected solution class

alternate_encodings.target: integration over the unit disk after y=x+c*t*z

excluded_degenerate_cases: t=0 is a limiting/boundary obligation, not direct substitution into the singular kernel. c=0 and c<0 are excluded. Weak/distributional solutions and bounded-domain boundary conditions are outside the provisional root.
